title: Nudges and Policy
welcome_lead: Thaler's nudges use behavioural insights to steer better choices.
meta_desc: A-Level Behavioural Economics: nudges and choice architecture.
final_note: Nudges respect freedom while exploiting predictable biases.

concepts.def: Small change in choice architecture that steers behaviour.
Way options are presented to decision makers.
Choice taken if no active selection is made.
Designing defaults that help but allow opt-out.
Co-author with Thaler on the book Nudge.

walkthroughs.body_html: Richard Thaler, 2017 Nobel laureate, argues small design changes - default opt-in to pension saving, smaller plates in canteens - can lift welfare without bans.
Changing the pension default from opt-in to opt-out lifts UK auto-enrolment rates from 60 percent to over 90 percent. Almost the same people in either case - but the default wins.
Critics call nudges manipulative and a distraction from structural reform. Supporters point to measurable gains at trivial cost - and the option to ignore the nudge.
